title: Sales partnership scratch notes - Acme Media (Noelle Kim)
content:
Account: Acme Media (digital publisher, programmatic ads + newsletter verticals)
Notes to self: pulled basic company info from Crunchbase and public blog posts. HQ: NYC. ~650 employees. Heavy traffic spikes during breaking news (ads + paywall auth). Likely using mix of cloud-managed inference and some in-house models for personalization. No public mention of dedicated LLM infra.

Key contacts (from LinkedIn + intros):
- Maria Gonzalez (Head of ML) – interested in personalization/recos; previous role at streaming company; likely cares about latency & cost.
- Daniel Park (Eng Manager, Ads infra) – cares about throughput, autoscaling, determinism.
- Priya Nair (Product, Reader Experience) – product metrics, retention tied to personalization quality.
- Purchased lists show CTO speaks to vendor selection. Try to get intro via Samir (has warm contact at Acme).

Why Redwood might matter to them:
- Predictable latency during spikes: Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity + burst can reduce tail latency during news spikes.
- Unit economics: batching + KV/prefix caching reduces per-token cost for personalization calls (large volume, short prompts).
- Rollouts + safety: our rollout + fallback policies help them A/B model variants without impacting live traffic.
- Private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) is attractive if they care about user data residency.

Observed pain signals (public / inferred):
- Multiple infra job postings for real-time personalization engineers (implies perf problems).
- Tweets about latency during breaking news (social engineers complaining about recos).
- Internal docs leaked: talk of cost blowouts on cloud GPU inference for peak hours.

Quick value props to call out in outbound:
- "Cut per-request latency tail by X% via dedicated routing + cache-aware serving" (don't promise numbers – use benchmark deck).
- "Lower per-token costs with workload-aware batching and quantization guidance – typical 20–40% savings in production pilots."
- "Can start hosted, then move to Dedicated/Private with same API and rollout tooling."

Outbound email drafts (short / cold):
Subject: Quick question about personalization latency at Acme\n
Hi Maria –
I’m Noelle on outreach at Redwood Inference. We help publishers reduce inference costs and tail latency for high-volume personalization without rewriting serving code.
We recently helped a publisher with similar traffic patterns move to a dedicated pool + prefix caching and reduced median latency and unit cost in production.
Would you be open to a 20-min intro next week to share the approach and see if there’s overlap?
— Noelle

Longer outbound (for Daniel / infra):
Subject: Predictable throughput for bursty inference at Acme

Hi Daniel,
I noticed Acme has big spikes around breaking news and you run real-time personalization – we work with infra teams to guarantee throughput and avoid costly overprovisioning. Redwood Dedicated provides reserved GPU capacity, autoscaling with burst, and automated fallback to smaller model variants when capacity is constrained.
Open to a short sync to review a throughput playbook + quick pricing model? Happy to include a technical lead.

LinkedIn connect message (short):
Hey Maria – curious if you’re seeing the same latency/cost tradeoffs others in publishing are seeing. Would love to swap notes if you have 10 mins.

Call / discovery script (bullet style):
- Quick intro (2min) – who we are, why outreach
- Current stack: what model(s) serve personalization? hosted vs self-hosted?
- Traffic profile: median qps, peak qps, seq length distribution, % of requests under 128 tokens
- Cost pain: cloud GPU spend? token-per-detail?
- SLOs: target p50/p95/p99 latency, incidents in last 6mo
- Rollouts: how do you handle model upgrades / A/B / canary?
- Security/compliance: data residency, PII handling, KMS/HSM needs
- Decision process: timeline, stakeholders, procurement needs
- Next steps: pilot proposal (4–6 weeks) or tech deep-dive with infra + ML

Objection handling (short bullets):
- "We host ourselves / comfortable with current infra" → acknowledge: great – ask about cost and ops burden. Pitch hybrid path: start with a small hosted experiment or co-located Dedicated region; emphasize same API and minimal code changes. Offer to share benchmarks from similar pub customers.
- "Latency is fine" → dig on tail vs median. Ask about p99 during spikes and if they’d like predictable tail without overprovisioning. Mention KV/prefix caching and routing policies reduce p99.
- "Budget / procurement complexity" → propose a short pilot with limited committed capacity; show pricing scenarios (monthly vs annual reserved) and highlight predictable cost model vs unknown cloud spend.
- "Security concerns / PII" → Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) + KMS/HSM integrations; offer SOC2/ISO docs and reference customers under NDA.

Pilot plan outline (for follow-up doc):
- Goals: Reduce p99 latency by X% (qualify on call) and demonstrable cost per request reduction
- Duration: 4–6 weeks
- Scope: X endpoints (personalization inference), sample traffic replay (we can help), no-prod integration step first
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens, error rates, quality delta vs baseline
- Deliverables: config suggestions (batching/quantization), rollout plan, final cost model and ops handoff

Notes / quick asks for internal next steps:
- Samir to intro to Maria (ask for warm intro by EOD) – Samir pinged in slack #partnerships 2026-02-18 (see thread).
- Prep short deck: 1-pager on Dedicated + caching + example savings. Owner: Harper – due 2026-02-24.
- Get sample traffic profile ask: median/peak qps, typical seq length distro, percent of requests <128 tokens. Owner: Noelle to request in intro email.
- Ask Solutions Eng to prepare minimal perf benchmarks for publisher workload (short prompts, high qps) – tag: SE-quick-bench.

Draft follow-up email (after intro call):
Subject: Next steps + pilot proposal

Thanks again for your time – as discussed, attached is a 1-pg pilot proposal and rough cost scenarios. Next suggested step: run a 4-week pilot on a small slice of traffic (we can help replay or run live with canary).

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Get Samir intro to Maria (urgent)
- [ ] Draft 1-pg pilot + pricing scenarios (Harper)
- [ ] SE perf bench (reach out to Samir/SE team)
- [ ] Update outreach cadences with short/long email options
- [ ] Save example benchmarks for publisher vertical (20–40% cost savings claim: need case study)

Random reminders: keep outbound short, call to action = 15–20m sync. Use customer stories vs numbers when cold; bring numbers after intro. Keep legal/compliance bits ready for CTO/Procurement.

Internal refs: Confluence partnership page (linked), JIRA ticket GTM-87 for pilot tracking, Slack #partnerships for intro thread.

— — End of scratch notes (will refine after sync).
